summary: Frontend-only test of Confort+ mobile deployment page (https://mobile-confort-build.preview.emergentagent.com/). The user-reported crash 'la version mobile plante en naviguant dans les menus de la palette' is REPRODUCED and ROOT CAUSED. The 10 read-aloud/contrast functional rules from the request COULD NOT be exercised because the testing methodology prescribed by the request (reading `window.readAloudServiceInstance`, `window.colorContrastServiceInstance`, etc. from page.evaluate) is NOT satisfied by this build: those const singletons are declared inside the module scope of /js/toolbar.min.js and are never attached to window (grep of toolbar.min.js: 0 matches for `window.readAloudServiceInstance`, only `window.__CONFORT_BASE__` is exposed). Driving the behaviour through the shadow-DOM palette UI is possible but does not expose `speakingElement` / `state` / `lastActionable` which the rules depend on. Main agent must either (a) add a tiny dev-only shim that attaches the five singletons to window (behind a build flag), or (b) rebuild toolbar.min.js with those symbols exported, so these rules can be verified deterministically.

ui_bugs.issue: REPRODUCED CRASH — 'palette plante en naviguant dans les menus'. During intensive navigation (open palette, click several buttons, close, re-open, 10-20 times), the app throws an uncaught `SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON` from `JSON.parse(...)` inside `HomeComponent.attributeChangedCallback`. Reproduction is 100% reliable in a fresh session after a few open/close cycles. The Emergent dev overlay then shows a 'Runtime error' modal that blocks the page. The root cause is in localStorage: the key `cplus-current-route` is written as the string literal `undefined` (not stringified JSON `null`), so when HomeComponent later observes an attribute change and calls `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('cplus-current-route'))` it blows up. Confirmed localStorage contents after the crash: `cplus-current-route: "undefined"` (raw text, not a JSON value). Two defects stacked: (1) RouteService / route observer writes `String(undefined)` into localStorage somewhere in the back-navigation path; (2) attributeChangedCallback does not guard against non-JSON values before calling JSON.parse.

integration_issues.flow: Read-aloud rules verification (rules 1-5) + reinforced contrasts non-regression
integration_issues.issue: Cannot be executed as prescribed: `readAloudServiceInstance`, `colorContrastServiceInstance`, `clickFaciliteServiceInstance`, `dragDropServiceInstance`, `clearlyLinksServiceInstance` are NOT on `window`. In /app/confort-src/src/app/core/services.core.ts they are declared `const readAloudServiceInstance = new ReadAloudService()` without any `window.readAloudServiceInstance = ...` or export. In the deployed bundle (/app/frontend/public/js/toolbar.min.js) grep returns 0 hits for `window.readAloudServiceInstance` and friends. Only `window.__CONFORT_BASE__` is exposed. Therefore the deterministic test strategy in the request (stub speechSynthesis.speak, call setReadAloud('sentence'), inspect speakingElement/state) is impossible on this build without changes.

action_items: FIX THE CRASH (highest priority) — guard `HomeComponent.attributeChangedCallback` so it never calls `JSON.parse` on a non-JSON string. Typical safe pattern: `const raw = newValue; if (raw == null || raw === 'undefined' || raw === 'null') return; try { const v = JSON.parse(raw); ... } catch { return; }`. Also fix the writer: find who writes `cplus-current-route` and make it never persist the literal 'undefined' (likely in route.service.ts: `localStorage.setItem('cplus-current-route', JSON.stringify(route ?? null))` — currently it probably passes `String(route)` and route is undefined at app start / after certain back navigations).

CLEAN UP localStorage on load — on first boot of HomeComponent, if `localStorage.getItem('cplus-current-route') === 'undefined'` then `localStorage.removeItem('cplus-current-route')`. This unblocks existing users without a hard reset.

ADD a dev/test hook so the five service instances can be reached from the page (needed to verify rules 1-5 and the image getInnerText rule). Minimal change in /app/confort-src/src/app/core/services.core.ts: `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.__CONFORT_BASE__?.exposeServicesForTests) { Object.assign(window, { readAloudServiceInstance, colorContrastServiceInstance, clickFaciliteServiceInstance, dragDropServiceInstance, clearlyLinksServiceInstance }); }` — gated so prod stays identical, enabled only when the deploy page sets the flag. Alternatively dispatch a `cplus:services-ready` CustomEvent on `window` carrying the instances in `event.detail`.

AFTER the two fixes above are deployed, re-run the full suite from the review request (sentence span wrapping including hyperlinks, click-on-link-inside-sentence does not navigate, Escape/contextmenu interruption, 1 s activation window, getImageText for alt / figcaption / 'absence de description', word-scope textContent preservation, reinforcedContrasts non-regression).
critical_code_review_comments: Robustness: any call to JSON.parse on a localStorage value must be wrapped in try/catch or guarded against the string 'undefined' / 'null'. This is a classic footgun and here it is the exact cause of the user-reported crash.

Encapsulation vs testability: the entire extension's service layer is module-private (good for prod) but the project's own test spec (this review request) assumes the singletons are reachable from the page. The two concerns need a dedicated test-only hook, not a change to the production surface.
localStorage write side: whoever writes `cplus-current-route` is clearly serialising `undefined` to the string 'undefined'. That value also leaks into any debug UI reading it back as a route name.

The crash is not caught by any top-level error boundary and is visible to the end user via the Emergent runtime-error overlay — in a real Firefox Android install this will manifest as a hard halt of the palette logic (listeners stop firing after the uncaught exception).

success_rate.frontend: crash reproduced + root-caused; functional read-aloud rules 1-5 not verifiable on current build

context_for_next_testing_agent: The crash is deterministic: viewport 390x844, load /, wait for cplus-app-root, click `#confort` inside its shadowRoot, click several of its inner `<button>`s, close, reopen ~5-10 times → `SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON` from HomeComponent.attributeChangedCallback @ toolbar.min.js:6:310454. localStorage.cplus-current-route === 'undefined'. Clear localStorage between tests. Once the dev shim for service instances is in place, the full read-aloud test matrix from the request can be executed with window.speechSynthesis.speak monkey-patched and `__spoken` collected.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE of the palette crash (user report: 'plante en naviguant dans les menus'): HomeComponent's observed attribute (likely the custom element attribute mirroring the current route) is updated on every navigation. Its `attributeChangedCallback` calls `JSON.parse(newValue)` without guarding. On certain back-navigation paths, the route value flowing in is the string literal 'undefined' (because somewhere in route.service.ts a route object is coerced via `String(route)` instead of `JSON.stringify(route)` before being written to the attribute / localStorage). JSON.parse('undefined') throws SyntaxError, the exception propagates uncaught and the Emergent overlay surfaces a 'Runtime error' modal, visually freezing the page. The persisted bad value in `localStorage['cplus-current-route']` means the crash can also fire on next page load if the stale value is reinjected into the attribute. Mitigation (two-line fix): sanitize both the writer (never persist non-JSON) and the reader (guard JSON.parse).
